SHAHEED MINAR
2014-02-04T00:00:53+06:00 | By Tasnima Haque Orin
https://www.thedailystar.net/shaheed-minar-9603

For the most part, Dhaka seems like a whirlpool of chaos, people and places. And the University of Dhaka campus stands as an exception. A sanctuary of greenery, young fresh faces discussing ideas and just chatting away, a place wrapped in nearly a century's worth of history, this place represents everything we hope for in our country. And these values drove so many to take a stance for their language 62 years ago. Everyone has seen honouring the martyrs of Ekushey February on television, but unless you visit the Shaheed Minar, tucked opposite the Mathematics building of Dhaka University in person, a lot is left unseen. Designed by Hamidur Rahman, this national monument represents a mother holding onto her sons who perished, as the rising sun shines on them. The 14 feet monument is the place for any national celebration, mourning, honouring and protest, and on any given day, you will come across people who take inspiration from our language heroes to voice their opinions. Nothing however, compares to the month of February, when the Shaheed Minar is repainted, redecorated, renovations done and ready to welcome the thousands of people observing the International Mother Language Day on 21 February -- the anniversary of the day in 1952 when students of DU laid down their lives for their language -- creating an amazing environment of solidarity and respect. Drop by at Shaheed Minar at any time of the year, be it a quick stop as part of your Dhaka University tour or on the way to Ekushey Boi Mela, when it's at its most festive. Whenever you do, you should visit it, because it doesn't cost a thing and because Shaheed Minar deserves to be visited and talked about and honoured, all through the year since the only way we can look into our future is by taking inspiration from our past.
